findings.evidence: Average.lean:184 `def azimuthalAverage ... := fun i x kT Q2 ζ => if kT < 0 then 0 else ...`; Average.lean:251 `simpa only [azimuthalAverage] using hite`. The PR already added `circleAverageTransverse_def` (Average.lean:93-98) for exactly this purpose, with a comment explaining the `(rfl)`; `azimuthalAverage` is the one definition in the PR without the counterpart.
findings.fix: Add `lemma azimuthalAverage_def (f : VectorTmd Flavor) (i : Flavor) (x Q2 ζ : ℝ) : (fun kT => azimuthalAverage f i x kT Q2 ζ) = fun kT => if kT < 0 then 0 else circleAverageTransverse (f i x · Q2 ζ) kT := (rfl)` — with the same `(rfl)` note as `circleAverageTransverse_def` — and rewrite with it in `regularity_azimuthalAverage` instead of `simp only [azimuthalAverage]`.
findings.issue: `azimuthalAverage` has no `_def` lemma, so the whole-function (`fun kT => ...`) form of a slice is unreachable through the API: `regularity_azimuthalAverage` closes its goal with `simpa only [azimuthalAverage] using hite`, i.e. by delta-unfolding the `@[expose]`d body. `azimuthalAverage_of_neg`/`_of_nonneg` are pointwise only and cannot produce the `ite`-form any measurability or continuity consumer needs.

findings.evidence: upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/CircleAverage.lean:217 `@[fun_prop] theorem Continuous.circleAverage {f : ℂ → E} (hf : Continuous f) : Continuous (Real.circleAverage f c)`; the attribute is already in use in this repo at EpsilonEridani/QFT/Scattering/DIS/Inclusive/CrossSection.lean:139,143.
findings.issue: `Continuous.circleAverageTransverse` is not tagged `@[fun_prop]`, although it is a direct transport of a Mathlib lemma that is, so `fun_prop` cannot discharge continuity of a transverse circle average even where it discharges the ℂ-sided original.

summary: The exported surface is now reachable and the circle-average transport is largely complete, but `azimuthalAverage` ships without a `_def`, so the file's own regularity proof delta-unfolds the exposed body instead of using the interface, and the continuity transport drops the `@[fun_prop]` tag its Mathlib original carries.
